dungeon.motif: surviving masonry and later roof damage

history.title: setup / foundation
history.account: Copper-Thread, acting for the Hollow Reed household, commissioned the fortress because people withdrawing from a nearby conflict needed a protected stopping point. The aim was to cover a retreat and shelter those left behind. The site was chosen because its position could control the approach without exposing every room to it.

history.title: e1 / transfer
history.account: The Hollow Reed household could no longer staff the place. They entrusted it to the incoming smuggler crew, who agreed to maintain the approach in exchange for use of the outer rooms, and moved out.

history.title: e2 / collapse
history.account: A weather-exposed support failed under load and broke a service crossing.

history.title: e3 / conceal
history.account: The incoming smuggler crew disguised the entrance to keep casual travelers away from the hazardous approach; those already living there retained the route.

history.title: e4 / repair
history.account: The incoming smuggler crew hired workers to repair the broken crossing.

history.title: e5 / survey
history.account: The incoming smuggler crew had the changed approaches surveyed so later visitors could distinguish old routes from surviving access.

history.title: e6 / move
history.account: The incoming smuggler crew moved a reserve of repair fittings from the protected dry store into the upper dry store to separate it from materials being issued for everyday use.

history.title: e7 / extend
history.account: The incoming smuggler crew employed builders to add space for a concealed trade base rather than dismantle the rooms still in use; the older access remained.
